summary: Phase 2 HibiscusPlus admin panel end-to-end tested. Backend: 17/17 pytest cases green (login happy/401/422, /me auth, /stats, recipes/products/blog CRUD, public regression, brute-force lockout). Frontend: admin login renders, failed login shows 'Invalid email or password' error text, successful login redirects to /admin dashboard with 5 stat tiles, token stored at localStorage['hp_admin_token'], ProtectedRoute bounces unauthenticated /admin back to /admin/login, /admin/recipes shows 12 rows, New drawer opens, creating TEST recipe adds row (12->13), deleting removes it (13->12), Sign Out clears token + redirects, View Site link has target=_blank to /. Public pages regression (/, /recipes, /blog, /markets, /breakfast, /feedback): all render with light cream theme bg rgb(250,245,238), footer + nav present, zero console errors. No test data leaked in recipes/products/blog collections.

minor.issue: Brute-force counter keys on request.client.host, but the Kubernetes ingress sends traffic through multiple proxy pods (seen: 10.208.133.82 and 10.208.150.130 alternating for the same caller). This effectively halves the per-key count and could let an attacker get ~10 attempts instead of 5 before lockout. Fix: honor X-Forwarded-For (left-most) or RFC 7239 Forwarded header when present, falling back to request.client.host. Lockout still triggers reliably when the ingress sticks to one IP (verified via keep-alive session), so this is a hardening item, not a breakage.

integration_issues.issue: Row is actually added to the table (12 -> 13) and DB persists, but the success toast with text 'Created.' was not detected in document body 2.5s after Save. Either the toast disappears too quickly (<2.5s) or uses a portal that is torn down immediately. Not blocking; cosmetic. Consider leaving toast visible >=3s or adding data-testid='toast-success' for easier verification.

action_items: (Hardening, P3) Change auth.py brute-force key to use X-Forwarded-For first-hop IP instead of request.client.host, so the ingress-rotated source IPs do not dilute the 5-attempt budget.
(Polish, P4) Add data-testid='toast-success' on the 'Created.'/'Updated.'/'Deleted.' toasts in AdminCrudPage and keep them visible for >=3s so automated tests can verify them.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 548 lines and mixes public recipes/products/blog/newsletter handlers with admin auth + CRUD. Consider splitting into routers (routers/public.py, routers/admin.py) once it crosses ~700 lines.

admin CRUD endpoints accept arbitrary dict payloads with no Pydantic validation per entity. This is an intentional trade-off per the brief (to let the frontend pass normalised lists), but it means no field-level constraints or type coercion at the API boundary. Add at least a soft `model_validate` step per entity for future safety.

auth.py in-memory _LOGIN_ATTEMPTS dict is process-local and unbounded (no TTL eviction for stale keys). Fine for single-admin v1 but should move to Redis/Mongo with a TTL index before horizontal scaling.

JWT is 24h with no refresh-token flow; a stolen token is valid for a full day with no server-side revocation. For single-admin v1 this is acceptable; document it and plan a revoke-list/rotating-secret story before multi-user.
Two duplicated feedback endpoints exist at /api/feedback (app.post + app.get) outside the api_router while everything else uses the router. Consolidate under api_router for consistency.

success_rate.frontend: 100% core flows (login/redirect/dashboard/CRUD add+delete/logout/protected route/view site) + 6/6 public pages regression

rca_of_issues.brute_force_dilution: Root cause: auth.py uses `request.client.host` for the brute-force key. Behind the Emergent ingress, outbound requests from a single caller are load-balanced across multiple proxy IPs (observed 10.208.133.82 and 10.208.150.130 alternating in backend.out.log for the same pytest run). Each IP has its own counter, so an attacker effectively gets N * 5 attempts where N = number of upstream proxies. Reproduction: `for i in 1..10; do curl -X POST .../api/admin/login -d '{email:e,password:wrong}'`. When curl keeps-alive on the same TCP, lockout hits at attempt 5 (verified). When each request opens a new TCP (python requests default), lockout took ~8-10 attempts in our run. Mitigation: in auth.py read `request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for', '').split(',')[0].strip()` first, then fall back to request.client.host.
rca_of_issues.create_toast_not_detected: Root cause: document.body.innerText was checked 2500ms after clicking Save, but row count had already updated — indicating the POST succeeded, the list refreshed, and the toast likely auto-dismissed in <2.5s. Not a functional bug; the create/delete themselves work. Mitigation: add data-testid on the toast and extend its visible duration to >=3000ms.
